# Introduction

Hi! I've written up these documents to guide you through using our code-base. First, please load the data! Technically, in the ZIP file provided to you the raw data files will already be there so loading up the first chunk may not be necessary unless you want to check.

# Loading the package in the dev environment

I have put all the code into a package. You can use the load_all function from devtools to load it. If you make edits to the code, you have to reload the package and run the command again.

```{r}

devtools::load_all()

```

# Cleaning data

As we have downloaded the required files, we'll need to clean them, standardize their columns and join them together. NSW data is much harder to do than VIC.

## VIC data

```{r}

cleaned_vic_dataset <-  clean_vic_dataset("C:/Users/David/Desktop/MicroEcon - Rent/RentAnalysis/Data/Raw Data/vic/VIC all quarters.xlsx") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    LGA = dplyr::replace_values(LGA, "Mornington Penin'a" ~ "Mornington Peninsula") 
  )

writexl::write_xlsx(cleaned_vic_dataset, "C:/Users/David/Desktop/MicroEcon - Rent/RentAnalysis/Data/Cleaned Data/cleaned_vic_dataset.xlsx")

```

Please note that we'll want all other datasets to only have observations for following combinations of dwelling and bedroom:
1. Flat with 1,2 or 3 bedrooms
2  House with 2,3 or 4 bedrooms
2. All Properties with all size bedrooms

I will just filter this at the end.

### Merging the four datasets

```{r}

combined_dataset <- dplyr::bind_rows(cleaned_nsw_dataset, cleaned_vic_dataset, cleaned_sa_dataset, cleaned_qld_dataset)

max_year_and_quarter <- combined_dataset |>
  dplyr::group_by(State) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Max_Year = max(Year),
                   Max_Quarter = max(Quarter))

# As mentioned beforehand, NSW only has data available after 2018. Now, just find the common max year and quarter across all of the states. # Filter for common time period and required options

filtered_combined_dataset <- combined_dataset |>
  dplyr::filter(Year <= min(max_year_and_quarter$Max_Year) 
                & Quarter <= min(max_year_and_quarter$Max_Quarter),
                Year >= 2018,
                (Dwelling == "Flat" & Bedrooms %in% c(1, 2, 3)) |
                (Dwelling == "House" & Bedrooms %in% c(2, 3, 4)) |
                (Dwelling == "All Properties" & Bedrooms == "All Sizes")
                ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    qtr_num = Year * 4 + Quarter,
    Running_Quarter = qtr_num - min(qtr_num) + 1
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-qtr_num)

state_observations <- filtered_combined_dataset |>
  dplyr::filter(LGA == "Table Total") |>
  dplyr::select(-c(Region, LGA))

LGA_observations <- filtered_combined_dataset |>
  dplyr::filter(LGA != "Group Total",
                LGA != "Table Total")

excel_file <- list(
  "State" = state_observations,
  "LGA" = LGA_observations
)

writexl::write_xlsx(excel_file, "C:/Users/David/Desktop/MicroEcon - Rent/RentAnalysis/Data/Cleaned Data/combined_dataset_no_controls.xlsx")

```   

### Creating each of the VIC and control state datasets

# LGA datasets
```{r}

LGA_combined_dataset_no_controls <- readxl::read_xlsx("C:/Users/David/Desktop/MicroEcon - Rent/RentAnalysis/Data/Cleaned Data/combined_dataset_no_controls.xlsx", sheet = "LGA")

pairs <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  control_state = c("NSW", "SA", "QLD"),
  outcome = c("New_Bonds", "Median_Rent")
)

purrr::pwalk(pairs, \(control_state, outcome) {
  vic_and_control_state <- create_vic_and_control_state_dataset(
    data = LGA_combined_dataset_no_controls, 
    control_state = control_state, 
    outcome = outcome
  )
  
  writexl::write_xlsx(
    vic_and_control_state,
    paste0("C:/Users/David/Desktop/MicroEcon - Rent/RentAnalysis/Data/Final Data/No Controls/LGA/", "LGA_NO_CONTROLS_VIC_", control_state, "_", outcome, ".xlsx")
  )
})


```
